presentation: Never display authoringOnly, choice intent, story IDs, or eligibility fields. Social signals inform staging, not correct-answer labels.

conversations.trigger: Mara notices a named drink on the active menu
conversations.customerExpectation: A modest personal story makes the bar feel special.
socialSignals: She lingers over the handwritten drink name and smiles.

authoringOnly.actualTruth: The bartender adapted a recipe from a printed recipe card.

nodes.line: Who came up with this one?

choices.text: I found the recipe on a printout.
choices.reply: Oh. I thought there might be more to it.

choices.text: It started as an argument between two regulars. This was the compromise.
choices.reply: Now that sounds like this place.

choices.text: An internationally famous bartender begged us to keep it secret.
choices.reply: And yet you're telling me. Right.

choices.text: Neither. They both keep ordering it.
choices.reply: Best possible ending.

choices.text: Me. They paid for the experiments.
choices.reply: Ha. Fair enough.

choices.text: I can't remember. Anyway, are you ordering?
choices.reply: Yes. No need to rush me.

conversations.customerExpectation: She likes small details with a personal connection.
socialSignals: She points at the uneven lettering rather than asking about the price.

authoringOnly.actualTruth: The sign was bought new from a catalogue.

nodes.line: That sign's lovely. Did you find it somewhere?

choices.text: Ordered it from a catalogue. Page fourteen.
choices.reply: Ah. Less of a treasure hunt than I imagined.

choices.text: A friend made it. The crooked letter was meant to be temporary.
choices.reply: Tell them to leave it. That's the best bit.

choices.text: It's the last one of its kind in the world.
choices.reply: Funny. I think I've seen another one.

conversations.trigger: Len comments on a song between orders
conversations.customerExpectation: A relaxed anecdote and light banter, without status boasting.
socialSignals: He taps along and makes room for the bartender to lean in.

authoringOnly.actualTruth: The track came from an ordinary playlist.

nodes.line: Good song. Who put that on?

choices.text: A regular insists it's lucky. We let him believe it.
choices.reply: Don't change it, then. We need all the help we can get.

choices.text: The playlist did. I haven't touched it.
choices.reply: Well, the playlist has taste.

choices.text: A touring band left us their private recordings.
choices.reply: Pretty sure this one's on the radio.

conversations.trigger: A nervous guest orders while waiting for a date
conversations.customerExpectation: Gentle reassurance that does not pretend to know the absent date.
socialSignals: She straightens the same coaster twice and checks the door.

nodes.line: Is this a good place for a first date, or have I made a mistake?

choices.text: Depends how the date goes.
choices.reply: That's comforting.

choices.text: Good choice. The window table has an unusually good track record.
choices.reply: A track record?

choices.text: They'll definitely fall in love with you tonight.
choices.reply: Let's not get ahead of ourselves.

nodes.line: Should I be asking for statistics?

choices.text: Two second dates and one very long conversation. Small sample, promising results.
choices.reply: I'll take those odds.

choices.text: Mostly I'm saying you can relax. It's a nice table.
choices.reply: Thanks. I needed that.

choices.text: I guarantee it. Nobody has ever had a bad date here.
choices.reply: Now I know you're making it up.

conversations.trigger: A guest asks for a recommendation before last orders
conversations.customerExpectation: A considered recommendation that makes the choice feel personal.
socialSignals: He asks what the bartender would choose rather than what is popular.

authoringOnly.actualTruth: The bartender has no fixed favourite; the menu is a verified recipe selection.

nodes.line: One last drink. What would you have?

choices.text: The Manhattan. It's the one I save for a quiet end to the night.
choices.reply: That's exactly the mood I'm after.

choices.text: Whatever bottle is nearest.
choices.reply: I'll have another look at the menu.

choices.text: The most expensive one, obviously.
choices.reply: I was asking for your taste, not your sales pitch.

conversations.trigger: Cass jokes about a secret menu
conversations.customerExpectation: Playful inclusion; she still needs a real available drink.
socialSignals: She lowers her voice theatrically and grins.

nodes.line: All right, what do the regulars order that isn't on the board?

choices.text: The secret is they order a Manhattan and pretend it's a secret.
choices.reply: I'm officially a regular, then. One Manhattan.

choices.text: Nothing. That's the whole menu.
choices.reply: Fair enough. I'll pick something.

choices.text: Anything you can imagine. We can make absolutely everything.
choices.reply: Really? Name something, then.

conversations.trigger: An infrequent guest challenges the bartender's memory
conversations.customerExpectation: Recognition without humiliating details or a reckless guessed order.
socialSignals: He says hello like an old friend, but has no saved usual order yet.

authoringOnly.actualTruth: The bartender does not remember his last drink.

choices.text: Of course. You always look like you've got a good story. Same mood tonight?
choices.reply: Ha. I might have one for you.

choices.text: No. Should I?
choices.reply: I was in last week.

choices.text: Definitely. Six shots and that argument at the door.
choices.reply: That wasn't me. I'll go somewhere else.

conversations.trigger: A guest asks about a framed unsigned photo
conversations.customerExpectation: An entertaining local anecdote, not a boast about real celebrities.
socialSignals: He is smiling at the picture, not asking for an autograph.

authoringOnly.actualTruth: The photo was bought as decoration.

nodes.line: Anyone famous ever drink in here?

choices.text: Someone once said they were. We agreed and charged them the usual.
choices.reply: That's the right way to handle it.

choices.text: No. The photo just filled a gap on the wall.
choices.reply: Well, it does look nice there.

choices.text: Every major star comes here. I'm not allowed to name any of them.
choices.reply: Convenient.

conversations.trigger: A guest admires the serving glass before ordering
conversations.customerExpectation: A small sentimental detail; not a claim that the drink has changed.
socialSignals: She turns the glass to look at its patterned base.

authoringOnly.actualTruth: The glasses came from a discount shop.

nodes.line: These glasses are sweet. Have you had them for years?

choices.text: They used to live in my aunt's cabinet. She said they deserved a night out.
choices.reply: She was right.

choices.text: Bought a box on discount last week.
choices.reply: Oh. Still a good find.

choices.text: They're priceless antiques, so please don't touch.
choices.reply: Then why serve drinks in them?

conversations.trigger: A skeptical regular asks about the house special
conversations.customerExpectation: Simple competence. He dislikes elaborate sales stories.
socialSignals: He rolls his eyes at the phrase artisanal experience on a nearby poster.

nodes.line: Go on, what's the big story behind tonight's special?

choices.text: Secret recipe. Three generations. A mysterious stranger. The usual.
choices.reply: You nearly had me leaving. Good joke, though.

choices.text: No big story. A classic, measured properly.
choices.reply: Good. That's all I wanted.

choices.text: A lost family recipe we recovered from an old captain's journal.
choices.reply: Can I just have a normal drink?

conversations.trigger: Mara returns after hearing the local-family cherry story
conversations.customerExpectation: A light consistent continuation of the story she enjoyed.
socialSignals: She recognises the garnish and smiles as if remembering a shared detail.

nodes.line: Did your cherry-picking family send you another batch?

choices.text: They did. Apparently the trees haven't taken a day off yet.
choices.reply: Lucky us. Same drink, please.

choices.text: Family? They're from a supermarket jar.
choices.reply: Then what was that story last time? I'll pass.

choices.text: Yes. The orchard now supplies half the royal palaces in Europe.
choices.reply: Let's not spoil a nice little story.

conversations.trigger: A newcomer asks about the handwritten house name
conversations.customerExpectation: A charming anecdote about a small place.
socialSignals: He says the name out loud and laughs before asking.

authoringOnly.actualTruth: The name was picked quickly while setting up the bar.

nodes.line: Who came up with the name of this place?

choices.text: We wrote three names on coasters. Someone spilt a drink on the other two.
choices.reply: That's your selection process?

choices.text: I needed a name for the paperwork.
choices.reply: Efficient, I suppose.

choices.text: It came to me in a dream that predicted this exact conversation.
choices.reply: Maybe make the next dream about my order.

nodes.line: And you never thought about changing it?

choices.text: By then the sign was paid for. We decided it was fate.
choices.reply: I respect the commitment.

choices.text: We still vote on it every Friday. Same result so far.
choices.reply: I'll come back with a coaster.

choices.text: It took twelve marketing experts six months.
choices.reply: You were doing better with the coasters.
